set.body:
Private cohort validation exposed a MultiMatch parity difference caused by exactly equal-cost optimal alignments. An independent 80-digit lattice calculation and an exact equal-squared-distance identity establish the tie. Both implementations minimize the stated cost, but their chosen correspondence changes the direction, length and position medians. Do not widen the numeric tolerance or declare eyesim the truth.

A fresh synthetic example reproduces the difference without copying private rows:
A positions: (100,100), (100,103), (104,106), onsets 0/150/300 ms.
B positions: (200,200), (201,205), (203,206), (208,206), onsets 0/150/300/450 ms.
All durations 100 ms; screen 1024x768; ungrouped baseline MultiMatch.
A movement vectors (0,3) and (4,3) are exactly equidistant from B's middle vector (2,1), making two paths optimal.
At eyes4s bbb9d49a, direction = 0.7951672353008665. At eyesim 36a96f962263a78de20dac010a8ec556e473e4fd (igraph from recorded local R session), direction = 0.937167041810999. Shape and duration agree. Both operand orders reproduce their respective result; identity comparisons return all ones in both.

Code seams: compare/.../Alignment.scala monotoneLattice traceback prioritizes diagonal/up/left; MultiMatch.scala takes component medians along that selected correspondence. eyesim creates a weighted lattice graph and accepts igraph shortest_paths' chosen path.

Acceptance: add the independently authored synthetic fixture and an independent optimal-path/cost oracle; make the MultiMatch tie-selection contract explicit, including operand symmetry and exact versus near ties; decide whether reference parity aligns tie policy or records a versioned convention distinction. Prove component reductions against the chosen path. Keep exact pair identities and original comparison discrepancies; a tied path is not a floating-point score-tolerance failure. Do not include private rows or screenshots in public fixtures. Scope broader Alignment behavior changes separately if the chosen policy affects DTW or Frechet clients.
set.title: MultiMatch: specify optimal-alignment tie policy and retain the parity distinction
